notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write the Psalm 7 notes. I didn't manage to read any of the approved sources before the tools stopped working, so I have nothing sourced to give you.

**What went wrong:**
1. My first attempt tried to open six pages directly: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible. All six were blocked. The tool only opens addresses that have first turned up in a search, and I hadn't searched yet.
2. I then started 12 searches covering the verse-by-verse commentaries, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, the NET notes, Augustine on New Advent, and key verses (v. 8 "according to my righteousness," v. 11 "indignation each day"). The tool refused to run them because I had used up its allowance for this session.

I won't fill the gap from my own memory, because your rules require every point to come from a page I actually read, with its URL.

**What I'd do next time:** search first, then open the pages the searches return. Here's the order I'd follow:
- **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word; Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Barnes on Bible Hub or StudyLight; Precept Austin; Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or Bible Hub).
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** likely v. 8 (claiming your own righteousness and integrity) and vv. 12–13 (on repenting). I'd check Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu against Reformed sources (Ligonier, Monergism, The Gospel Coalition) and Lutheran ones (1517.org, LCMS).
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes on "Shiggaion" and on God's indignation in v. 11; Augustine's *Expositions on the Psalms* on New Advent; anything on catholic.com or oca.org.

If you start a new message (even just "go ahead"), I'll run those searches and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after every point.
